> I think this issue covers the core missing capability. I would like to add a related runtime-sandbox use case that may affect where the API should live.
> 
> Runtime use case
> 
> A security plugin such as opencode-landstrip can sandbox each Bash tool call with Landlock, seccomp, Seatbelt, or AppContainer.
> 
> Some permissions cannot be determined in tool.execute.before. The sandbox only discovers the actual resource after the process starts, for example when seccomp intercepts:
> 
> openat("/home/user/.ssh/config") connect("127.0.0.1:5432")
> 
> The sandbox broker must hold that operation, request approval through OpenCode, and then resume or deny the operation.
> 
> Today, opencode-landstrip handles this through a TUI-specific dialog. That works in the official TUI, but SDK clients such as OpenChamber cannot render the prompt without Landstrip-specific integration.
> 
> Current API status
> 
> OpenCode already contains most of the required pieces:
> 
> Plugin-defined tools receive an awaitable context.ask(). The internal v2 permission service provides assert(), which evaluates policy and waits for a reply when the result is ask. The v2 SDK exposes session.permission.create(). Standard permission requests already have events, pending-request listing, and reply APIs.
> 
> However:
> 
> tool.execute.before does not receive the same permission capability as a plugin-defined tool. A server plugin cannot access an awaitable permission requester outside its own custom tool body. session.permission.create() returns { id, effect } immediately. A plugin must implement its own event subscription, deferred map, cancellation, reconnect handling, and cleanup to wait for the reply. The injected PluginInput.client still uses the legacy SDK client, while the v2 client is a separate export.
> 
> related: [landstrip/landstrip#52](https://github.com/landstrip/landstrip/issues/52)
> 
> I might add more thoughts here.

There is a semantic difference with the permissions:

1. Agent permissions are actually pre-launch permissions.
2. Sandbox permissions are actually post-launch permissions.

It is also good to keep in mind that:

1. Agent permissions cannot be described with sandbox policy.
2. Sandbox permissions cannot be described with agent permissions.

Finally, consider this:

1. Agent permissions define permissions for a primary or subagent.
2. Sandbox permissions act on tool commands.

Sandbox permissions need to be separate too because agent permissions we can predict but tool commands can be any possible random executable; or even malware. Malware and other misbehaving executable are the root reason why the sandbox makes sense in the first place.

Thus, also permission queries emit from exactly two **disjoint** stimulis:

1. A primary or subagent definition with "ask" permissions.
2. Tool-command doing something that requires a permission.

So I'm not sure what the correct actions are, just underlying important details and differences.

Still present in 1.18.8 (macOS, Apple Silicon). Reproduces on home and Settings.

Root cause looks like #38055 (draggable project rows), which introduced `AutoScroller` from `@dnd-kit/dom`. In `@dnd-kit/solid@0.5.0`, `DragDropProvider` reassigns `_manager.plugins` from a `createEffect`, which drops the core plugins — so `Scroller` is gone by the time `AutoScroller` registers against it.
